paper.title: Learning Unknown Service Rates in Queues: A Multi-Armed Bandit Approach

settings.name_in_paper: Queueing bandit: single queue with K servers
unmapped: State-dependent objective: jobs arrive Bernoulli(lambda) to a queue Q(t)=(Q(t-1)+A(t)-S(t))^+; reward (departure) accrues only when the queue is non-empty; performance is queue-regret Psi(t)=E[Q(t)-Q*(t)] at time t versus a genie always choosing the best server (not cumulative regret)
Server service outcomes are i.i.d. Bernoulli(mu_k); stability lambda < mu* (load eps = mu* - lambda > 0)
settings.definition_quote: arrivals to the queue and service offered by the servers are according to a product Bernoulli distribution, i.i.d. across time slots, with arrival probability $\lambda$ and service probabilities given by the vector $\bm{\mu}$ ... We assume that the system can be stabilized if the best server is known a priori, i.e., $\lambda < \mu^*$. ... $Q(t) = ( Q(t-1) + A(t) - S(t) )^+$.

settings.name_in_paper: Queueing bandit: multi-queue switch network (U queues, K servers, matchings) with unique optimal matching
unmapped: State-dependent objective: per-queue queue-regret Psi_u(t)=E[Q_u(t)-Q*_u(t)] where queues evolve with Bernoulli arrivals and services; departures only when queue non-empty
Unique optimal matching (Assumption 1) and stability eps_u = mu*_u - lambda_u > 0 for all queues (Assumption 2)
Learner knows number of queues U and the set of matchings
settings.definition_quote: The multi-queue switch network consists of $U$ queues and $K$ servers, where $U \leq K$. ... Arrivals to queues and service offered by the links are according to product Bernoulli distribution and i.i.d. across time slots. ... The task is to schedule, in every time slot, a matching in the complete bipartite graph between queues and servers.

source.quote: For any problem instance $(\pmb{\lambda}, \pmb{\mu})$, any queue $u \in [U]$, any $\beta < 2$, $\gamma > \frac{\beta}{\beta - 1}$, $\delta > \beta$, there exists a constant $C$ independent of $K$ and $\epsilon_u$ ... such that ... $$\Psi_u(t) \leq \frac{289 K \log^3 t}{\epsilon_u^2 t}$$ $\forall t \geq C \max \left\lbrace \left( \frac{1}{\epsilon_u} \right)^{\gamma}, \left( \frac{K}{\epsilon_u} \right)^{\beta} , K^{2\delta} \right\rbrace$.

source.quote: Given any single queue system $(\lambda,\pmb{\mu})$, and for any $\alpha$-consistent policy and $\gamma > \frac{1}{1 - \alpha}$, there exist constants $\tau$ and $C$ ... if $\epsilon < \eta$, then the regret $\Psi(t)$ satisfies $\Psi(t) \geq \frac{D(\pmb{\mu})}{2} (K-1) \frac{\log t}{\log \log t}$ for $t \in \left[ \max \{C K^{\gamma }, \tau \}, (K-1)\frac{D(\pmb{\mu})}{2\epsilon} \right]$.

bound.regime: eps_u < eta and t in [max{C_1 K^gamma, tau}, (K-1) D_mu/(2 eps_u)]

source.label: thm:lb-early-multiq
